entry.title: Say Goodbye to One-by-One Replication Task Creation! 👋
entry.content:
200 Replication Tasks in 30 Minutes? Sounds Crazy… Right? 😄

But what if I tell you it’s actually possible?

While working with Smart Data Integration (SDI) / SAP HANA CLOUD / SAP Business Application Studio (BAS), I came across a very practical challenge:

👉 Creating replication tasks individually can become extremely time-consuming.

Now imagine a scenario where you need to create 200 replication tasks.

That could mean:
⏳ 100+ hours of manual effort
👥 Multiple colleagues involved
🔄 Repetitive activities
😓 Higher chances of manual errors

And then I asked myself:

“Why should we create them one by one when most of the required information is already available in the source system?” 🤔

That question led me to build an automation flow for replication task creation. ⚙️

🔍 The approach

A replication task essentially requires information such as:

📌 Table & column details
📌 Data types and lengths
📌 Primary key information
📌 Nullable / non-nullable attributes
📌 Source & target table names
📌 Remote Source name
📌 Source Schema name

So instead of manually entering this information:

Source System → SQL Query → Metadata Extraction → Automation Script → Replication Tasks 

The flow is:

1️⃣ Fetch all required metadata from the source system using SQL queries.

2️⃣ Process the extracted information through an automation script.

3️⃣ Generate the required replication task definitions automatically — whether it’s 1, 100, 200 or even 1,000+ tasks.

4️⃣ The automation can be implemented directly through SAP Business Application Studio, or extended into a CAPM application for a more user-friendly and scalable solution.

⚡ The result?

Instead of spending 100+ hours creating 200 replication tasks manually…

👉 ~30 minutes to generate them through automation.

That's not just automation. That's turning repetitive manual effort into a scalable process. 💡

And the best part?

This approach can be extended further to introduce validations, error handling, monitoring and potentially even end-to-end automated onboarding of tables.

Would you be interested in seeing how the automation works under the hood? 👀

#SAPHANA # SAPHANACLOUD #SAPBusinessApplicationStudio  #CAPM  #Automation #Replication #SAPBTP #HANACloud #TechInnovation#SDI #SmartDataIntegration

entry.title: Maintain outgoing EDI-connection data for partner while processing PO Change (ZNEC / ORDCHG )
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I am configuring outbound EDI for Purchase Order Change in SAP S/4HANA.

Requirement:

  • PO Creation:
    • Output Type: ZNEU
    • Message Type: ORDERS
    • Basic Type: ORDERS05
  • PO Change:
    • Output Type: ZNEC
    • Message Type: ORDCHG
    • Basic Type: ORDERS05

When I change the PO quantity, the Output Type ZNEC is successfully determined and triggered in the PO output. However, while saving the Purchase Order, SAP raises the following error before creating the outbound IDoc:

VN032 - Maintain outgoing EDI-connection data for partner 20020506.

Even when I click Processing Log for the ZNEC output, the same error is displayed.

I have already verified the following:

  • WE20 partner profile is maintained for partner 20020506.
  • Partner Type = LI.
  • Partner Role = VN.
  • Outbound parameters are maintained for:
    • ORDERS → ORDERS05 (for New ZNEU) - Process code ME10
    • ORDCHG → ORDERS05 (for Change ZNEC)
  • Receiver Port is maintained.
  • Process Code is maintained (ME11 for ORDCHG).
  • Message Control is maintained:
    • Application = EF
    • Output Type = ZNEC
    • Process Code = ME11
  • Output condition record (MN05) is maintained.
  • Partner Function in the condition record = VN.
  • Partner Function in the Output Type = VN.
  • Partner Role in WE20 = VN.
  • The output record (ZNEC) is successfully created when the PO is changed.

Despite all the above configurations, SAP still throws VN032 before creating the outbound IDoc.

Has anyone encountered this issue? Is there any additional configuration, table, runtime check, or enhancement that I should verify for partner profile determination?

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

NW ABAP Integration Technology (ALE) MM (Materials Management) Sourcing and Procurement - Purchase Contract Management MM Purchasing SAP NetWeaver Application Server for ABAP Basis Technology SAP ERP for Business All-in-One, manufacturing edition  #ORDERS05 #IDOC

entry.title: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – J1IG STO BAdI: GR Validation and Reference Number Change Not Work
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

We have a requirement in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition related to the India GST STO process.

Application:

Create Inbound Invoices for STOs – India (J1IG / J_1IG_INV)

We are using:

  • BAdI: BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD

  • Method: CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

  • Custom Implementation: YY1_STO_CLOUD

We have two requirements, but currently neither requirement is working as expected.

Requirement 1 – Block J1IG if GRN is not posted

J1IG should not allow creation/posting of the inbound GST invoice/FI vendor document if the STO PO does not have a valid Goods Receipt.

Expected behavior:

STO PO → GR 101 → J1IG Inbound GST Invoice

If Movement Type 101 has not been posted, J1IG should stop the process with an error.

Also, if 101 was posted and completely reversed by 102, it should not be considered a valid GR.

We attempted to implement this validation in:

BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD → CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

However, J1IG is still proceeding even when the required GR has not been posted.

Requirement 2 – Change J1IG Reference Number

Currently, when we click Create Inbound GST Invoice in J1IG, the Reference Number is automatically populated with the ODN / GST Sequence Number.

Current:

Reference Number = ODN / GST Sequence Number

Required:

Reference Number = STO Outbound Billing Document Number

The required billing document is the STO Billing – GST Out. Inv. document.

We attempted to change this using:

BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD → CHANGE_BEFORE_POST

However, the ODN number is still being populated and the STO billing document number is not appearing.

Our question

Could an SAP expert please advise:

  1. Is BADI_J_1IG_STO_CLOUD / CHANGE_BEFORE_POST the correct BAdI to implement both requirements?

  2. How can we check for a valid 101 GR not completely reversed by 102 in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?

  3. How can we stop J1IG posting from this BAdI when GR is missing?

  4. Which exact field/structure controls the J1IG Reference Number?

  5. Is there another released BAdI/API required to replace the ODN with the STO billing document number?

  6. Is the Reference Number overwritten by standard J1IG processing after CHANGE_BEFORE_POST?

We are looking for a released/clean-core solution for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

We can provide our current YY1_STO_CLOUD implementation and screenshots if required.

Thank you.

entry.title: AUTHORITY-CHECK returns values not maintained in Business Role – SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
We are working on the FG (Finished Goods) screen in SAP Public Cloud, where we need to control authorization based on different fields and operations.

One of the fields in the FG screen is a Shift dropdown. This dropdown has 3 possible values:

  • DAY – Day Shift
  • NGT – Night Shift
  • GEN – General Shift

The requirement is that the user should only be authorized for the Shift values that are maintained in their Business Role.

For example, suppose a Business Role has the following authorization:

Application: FG
Operation: 0010
Shift: GEN

In this case, when the user accesses the FG screen, the expected authorization should be:

  • GEN → Authorized
  • DAY → Not Authorized
  • NGT → Not Authorized

Technically, we have created a Global Authorization Class for performing the authorization checks, a Field-Level Authorization Class for checking authorization for individual fields, and a Behavior Implementation Class that calls these authorization methods and returns the result to the FG screen.

The issue we are facing is with the actual authorization check.

During debugging, we are checking each Shift value separately. For example:

GEN → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

This is correct because GEN is assigned in the Business Role.

But when we check:

DAY → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

and

NGT → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

These are also returning authorized, even though DAY and NGT were not assigned in the Business Role.

We also tested the standard AUTHORITY-CHECK directly during debugging, without using our authorization wrapper method. Even there, DAY and NGT are returning:

sy-subrc = 0

So it does not appear to be an issue with our wrapper logic or with assigning rv_ok = X.

We are seeing the same type of behavior with some of the other authorization fields as well: values that are not explicitly maintained in the Business Role are still passing the authorization check.

1.Global class -   METHOD can_work_on.

  IF iv_inchg IS NOT INITIAL

     AND iv_machine IS NOT INITIAL

     AND iv_biltyp IS NOT INITIAL.

    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'ZPP_PRDEXE'

      ID 'ZPPAPP'   FIELD iv_app

      ID 'ZPPOPER'  FIELD iv_oper

      ID 'ZPPSHIFT' FIELD iv_shift

      ID 'ZPPINCHG' FIELD iv_inchg

      ID 'ZPPMACH'  FIELD iv_machine

      ID 'ZPPBLTYP' FIELD iv_biltyp.

  ELSE.

 

    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'ZPP_PRDEXE'

      ID 'ZPPAPP'   FIELD iv_app

      ID 'ZPPOPER'  FIELD iv_oper

      ID 'ZPPSHIFT' FIELD iv_shift

      ID 'ZPPINCHG' DUMMY

      ID 'ZPPMACH'  DUMMY

      ID 'ZPPBLTYP' DUMMY.

  ENDIF.

  rv_ok = xsdbool( sy-subrc = 0 ).

ENDMETHOD.

 

2.Behaviour Class - DATA(lv_gen_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'GEN' ).

      DATA(lv_day_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'DAY' ).

      DATA(lv_ngt_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'NGT' ).

      ls_result-ShiftGeneralAuth = lv_gen_auth.

      ls_result-ShiftDayAuth     = lv_day_auth.

      ls_result-ShiftNightAuth   = lv_ngt_auth.

entry.title: Graph-Based RAG Solution with SAP HANA Cloud Discovery Agents
entry.content:
Context

This article presents practical insights from the SAP Beta Program for SAP HANA Cloud Data and Discovery Agents. The solution combines SAP HANA metadata, knowledge graphs, and vectorized summaries to enable natural-language discovery across semantically related database tables. The exercise involved configuring SAP AI Core connectivity, certificates, triple-store and NLP capabilities, graph-based RAG structures, and role-based access for administrative and agent users. The beta demonstrated promising potential for simplifying data exploration across complex SAP HANA models, while also highlighting important considerations around setup complexity, security privileges, metadata quality, and memory consumption. Further validation is recommended to assess scalability, accuracy, governance, and production readiness.

Background of the Beta Program

This article is based on my participation in the SAP Beta Program for SAP HANA Cloud Data and Discovery Agents.

The purpose of the program was to evaluate new procedures and tools capable of identifying semantic relationships and generating summaries used to respond to natural language queries spanning multiple tables.

The project involves building a graph-based RAG dataset from SAP HANA metadata, where database objects and relationships are represented in a knowledge graph, and summaries are vectorized into a RAG table for semantic retrieval and natural language querying.

The goal was to prepare the HANA Cloud instance with SAP AI Core, configure certificates, and activate settings to facilitate the discovery agents.

Setup

High-Level Architecture

Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

Flow:

User Query → Discovery Agent → SAP AI Core Model → RAG Retrieval & Knowledge Graph → SAP HANA Tables → Response

Prerequisites

  1. Enable Triple Store and NLP:

Note: NLP activation may lead to an increased memory footprint.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

2. An AI Core instance with the deployment URL:

Configure an AI Core Instance:

  • Go to ML Operations > Deployment and create a new deployment configuration.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

  • Select the deployment configuration to retrieve the Deployment URL.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

3. Create Personal Security Environment (PSE) Store and Root Certificates:

  • Follow the SAP AI Core Service Key Setup Guide to create the PSE.
  • Modify the JSON configuration to extend validity to 60 days.
{
  "xsuaa": {
    "credential-type": "x509",
    "x509": {
      "key-length": 2048,
      "validity": 60,
      "validity-type": "DAYS"
    }
  }
}
  • Note: Need a user with DBADMIN privileges (or execution via the DBADMIN user) to run the required SQL statements.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

Confirm Setup:

  • Execute the confirmation procedure:

CALL "Get_Remote_Source_AI_Models"('DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE', ?);

Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

Execution

The project includes code setup with synthetic data for tables loaded into the HANA DB via DBX. Python scripts were configured in VS Code to perform the following steps:

  1. Metadata File: Create a metadata file listing the database objects.

 

2. Environment Variables: Set the required environment variables:

set HANA_HOST=<hana_cloud_instance_id>.hanacloud.ondemand.com
set HANA_USER=<agent_admin_user>
set HANA_PASSWORD=<agent_admin_user_password>
set HANA_AGENT_RAG_TOOL=true
set HANA_AGENT_STRUCTURED_PROMPT=true
set HANA_AGENT_USE_TABLE_INFORMATION_TOOL=true
set HANA_AGENT_USE_RELATED_OBJECTS_TOOL=true
set HANA_AGENT_USE_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_TOOL=true
set HANA_AGENT_USER_SQL_FILTER_VERIFICATION_TOOL=true
set TRACE_LEVEL=debug
  • Graph Creation: Create the DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA and run create_graph.py:
python src/graph/create_graph.py --knowledgeGraphName DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM --ragSchemaName DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA --ragTableName DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX "<file_path>obj_infos\aiEnabledObjects_EPM_ALL.yaml"
  • Agent User Permissions: Grant execution privileges for the required procedures:
  • SYS.DATA_AGENT_DEV
  • SYS.DISCOVERY_AGENT_DEV
  • Resource Access: Grant access to the remote source, knowledge graph, and RAG table:
GRANT EXECUTE ON REMOTE SOURCE <remote_source> TO <user>;
GRANT SPARQL QUERY TO <user>;
CALL SPARQL_EXECUTE('GRANT SELECT ON <HANA_OBJECTS> TO <user>', '', ?, ?);
GRANT SELECT ON "<schema>"."RAG" TO <user>;
  • Role & User Configuration:

AI_ADMIN_ROLE andAI_ADMIN_USER to:

  • Create remote source
  • Create index structures (Object Knowledge Graph, RAG table)
  • Create wrapper procedures
  • Grant privileges to AI_AGENT_USER

AI_AGENT_USER to:

  • EXECUTE permissions for the remote source
  • READ permissions for index structures
  • EXECUTE permissions for wrapper procedures
  • READ permissions for sample data tables

Test Results

Invoke the procedure and monitor the query execution results.

CALL SYS.DISCOVERY_AGENT_DEV (
    'In which position does Mia Nguyen work?',
    '{
        "remoteSourceName":"DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE",
        "knowledgeGraphName":"DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM",
        "ragSchemaName":"DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA",
        "ragTableName":"DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX"
    }',
    ?
);
To answer the question "In which position does Mia Nguyen work?", here is how you can find the answer using the available HANA database objects:
 
1. The table "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees" contains employee information, including first and last names, and an "OrgUnitId" column that links each employee to an organizational unit.
2. The table "EPM_DATA"."OrgUnits" contains organizational unit information, including "OrgUnitId" and "OrgUnitName". The "OrgUnitName" typically represents the department or position name.
 
Although the sample data does not include "Mia Nguyen", you can use the following approach to find the position for any employee:
 
- Look up the employee in "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees" by matching "FirstName" and "LastName" to "Mia" and "Nguyen".
- Retrieve the corresponding "OrgUnitId" for that employee.
- Join this "OrgUnitId" with "EPM_DATA"."OrgUnits" to get the "OrgUnitName", which represents the position or department.
 
Here are the relevant columns:
 
From "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees":
- "FirstName" (
CALL SYS.DATA_AGENT_DEV (
    'In which position does Mia Nguyen work?',
    '{
        "remoteSourceName":"DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE",
        "knowledgeGraphName":" DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM ",
        "ragSchemaName":"DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA",
        "ragTableName":" DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX "
    }',
    ?
);
Press enter or click to view image in full size

 

Observations & Key Learnings

  • Entry Point: Setting up the SAP AI Core instance and Deployment URLs is the necessary starting point.
  • Memory Footprint: Enabling Triple Store noticeably increases memory consumption.
  • Graph Modeling: Defining proper table linkages inside the Knowledge Graph YAML file is crucial for cross-table relationships.
  • Privilege Management: Explicitly grant table data schema privileges to the execution user.
  • Natural Language Querying: Demonstrates strong potential for running complex queries across semantically related tables using plain language.

Thank you to the HANA Cloud team from India and Germany who facilitated this program.
